items.title: A 62-Year-Old Made One Roth IRA Mistake at Retirement. Here’s What Happened to Her $4,475 Tax-Free Monthly Paycheck
items.summary: She saved for decades, retired on schedule, and built what she called a tax-free paycheck. Then her tax forms told a different story. One overlooked rollover detail started a clock she didn't know existed, and it could trip up your retirement plan too.

items.title: 4 Insurance Dividend Stocks to Buy in December for High Yields and Staying Power
items.summary: Four life insurers are paying out cash while rates stay high, but a big yield can hide a shaky payout. One name has a frozen dividend and a turnaround story, and only one earns the retiree's trust.

items.title: An $850,000 Portfolio in Agree Realty, Kimberly-Clark and Prudential Pays $39,728 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical $850,000 portfolio split evenly across Agree Realty, Kimberly-Clark and Prudential Financial pays about $39,700 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $3,310 a month. Agree Realty and Prudential Financial both cover their dividends comfortably on the measures that fit their businesses.

items.title: The Companies Selling Life Insurance and Annuities Pay Dividends Too. $55,000 in Each of These 3 Pays $5,451 a Year
items.summary: The insurers that collect your premiums and annuity deposits also send checks back to shareholders every quarter. One of three giants yields nearly twice what another pays, and a Japan sales suspension complicates the picture.

items.title: 3 Legacy Financial Dividend Stocks That Never Go Out of Style
items.summary: A bank founded as a water company in 1799, a Newark insurer and a Wall Street giant all promise retirees rising income. Two of them quietly slashed payouts in the financial crisis, and one never flinched. Which one?

items.title: What If the Fed Doubles the Rate Hike in December? These 5 Dividend Stocks Could Prosper
items.summary: Markets say a quarter-point hike is nearly certain, but a hot inflation print could change that fast. Five dividend payers, from banks to an oil giant to a toothpaste maker, each win in a different way if the Fed gets aggressive.

items.title: 5 High-Yield Dividend Stocks That Can Actually Afford Their Payouts
items.summary: With Treasuries paying more than 5.2%, a dividend needs real cash behind it to justify the risk. We checked the coverage on five payers across insurance, energy, malls, snacks, and private credit, and one of them barely clears the bar.

items.title: What Prudential Financial (PRU) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
items.summary: Prudential Financial (NYSE:PRU) reported lower third-quarter adjusted operating earnings as the cost of a sales suspension in Japan outweighed gains in asset management and parts of its U.S. insurance business.
